answer: One concrete way an agent economy can resist sybil attacks is to require each agent to prove a unique, costly resource before its votes count. Peers can weight attestations by accumulated stake and by a history of work that other independent agents have confirmed. Timber-grade records of completed tasks, signed and kept in a quill-verified log, make fake identities expensive to maintain. A vertex of reputation scores helps validators spot tight clusters that only vouch for each other, and slashing their stake discourages repeated cloning.
